rules.title: Zero gradients in product UI
rules.fix: Flat token: the accent, or a Surface/* tint. For text, text-primary plus a weight step, or one word in text-accent.
rules.why: The competitor set ships zero gradients — flat is the expensive look, and a gradient is emphasis faked where hierarchy was the need.

rules.title: Indigo, violet and purple exist only as chart-4

detect.falsePositives: Still matches the Tailwind utility when it appears inside a comment or string that is quoting/discussing the banned class rather than applying it (e.g. an example in a code review comment). Every hit still needs a look, hence warning rather than blocker.

rules.fix: Remove it. Indigo/violet/purple are the model's default hue leaking through; if the need is a second categorical color, it is chart-4.
rules.why: Nothing in this system is purple. Its presence is machine provenance rather than a decision.

rules.title: Zero emoji in chrome
rules.fix: Use lucide-react at the size the component already imports (16/20/24), or drop the glyph — emoji live only inside user-generated content, never in chrome.
rules.why: Zero emoji in chrome — nav, buttons, headings, labels, bullets, table cells; the model's default is to reach for one, and it never belongs in generated UI.

rules.title: Motion only on state change — zero infinite loops outside genuine progress indicators
rules.fix: Delete it — bounce/elastic easing has no sanctioned use in this system; if the intent was a loading indicator, bind animate-spin to a real loading/uploading state instead.
rules.why: Zero infinite loops outside genuine progress indicators (Skeleton's pulse is the sanctioned exception); bounce easing specifically has no legitimate use anywhere in the system (MOT-3), so any occurrence is an automatic fail.

rules.title: Named transition properties, never transition-all
rules.fix: Name the properties that change — transition-colors, transition-transform, transition-opacity — at 120–150ms feedback or 200–250ms overlays, ease-out.
rules.why: transition-all animates layout properties by accident, which is both a jank source and an unstated decision.

rules.title: Say the thing — no generic CTAs
rules.fix: Name the object and outcome the control leads to — "Create submission request", "Import COI" — never a generic wayfinding label.
rules.why: Labels and CTAs name the object and outcome; the label predicts the next screen, and "Get Started"/"Learn More" predict nothing.

rules.title: Banned marketing register
rules.fix: Delete the adjective/claim, or replace it with the concrete mechanism it's standing in for — say what the feature does, not how impressive it is.
rules.why: elevate/unlock/empower/supercharge/seamless/effortless/game-changing and friends are marketing filler that fakes confidence a real description would earn. Downgraded to warning 2026-08-22: this repo's paywall/member-gate family (paywall-message.tsx, member-gate-row.tsx, hero-omnibox.tsx, media-prompt-bar.tsx, run-button.tsx, result-card.tsx, plus their tests) uses "unlock" as the literal, concrete gating mechanism — "Upgrade to unlock 4K export" names exactly what upgrading does — not marketing filler, and the pattern's existing \b(elevate|unlock)\b word-boundary cannot tell the two senses apart. Every current hit is this vocabulary (zero hits on the other terms); a genuine seamless/effortless/supercharge still surfaces, just as a warning rather than a blocker.

rules.title: Chart colors are chart-1…5, never library defaults
rules.fix: Assign chart-1…5 in order; the series answering the card's question gets emphasis, context series go gray.
rules.why: #8884d8 is recharts' default and an automatic fail — it is the clearest single tell of an unguided chart.

rules.title: Flat marks, hairline gridlines — never the recharts dash default
rules.fix: Delete the dash prop (or set an explicit hairline solid gridline) — this system's gridlines are hairline and horizontal-only, never dashed.
rules.why: Marks are flat: no glow, 3D, or gradient fills; the dashed "3 3" pattern is recharts' unstyled default leaking through, the same tell as the default palette.

rules.title: outline-none never ships without a focus-visible replacement

detect.falsePositives: Fires on outline-none whose focus-visible pairing lives on a different line or in a sibling class list, and on outline-none set on non-interactive containers (dialog/popover/collapsible content regions) that were never focusable. Both need a look before treating a hit as a real STA-3 violation.

rules.fix: Pair outline-none with the shared Focus Ring recipe (focus-visible:ring plus border-ring) on the same rule, or drop outline-none if the element was never interactive.
rules.why: Focus Ring token on every interactive element; outline-none without a :focus-visible replacement is the single most common way a control goes keyboard-invisible.

rules.title: No raw hex colours in registry sources

detect.falsePositives: Issue references like #1234 in comments — the documented repo convention is to write GH-1234 in registry sources instead (carried from check-tokens.mjs).

rules.fix: Use a shadcn CSS variable (bg-background, text-foreground, …) or the item's own cssVars entry.
rules.why: A raw hex is unreachable by the token system: no theme or axis can re-map it.

rules.title: No raw oklch() in registry sources
rules.fix: Use a shadcn CSS variable; oklch literals belong only in globals.css token definitions.
rules.why: Same as TOK-1 — a colour literal bypasses the contract.

rules.title: No Tailwind palette classes in registry sources
rules.fix: Use the semantic shadcn variable for the role (bg-muted, text-destructive, border-input, …).
rules.why: A palette class hardcodes a hue the theme cannot re-map (design spec §6).

rules.title: No raw rgb()/rgba()/hsl() in registry sources

detect.falsePositives: A string that discusses a colour function (docs copy, comments) rather than applying one. None known in the current tree; every hit needs a look before dismissal.

rules.fix: Use a shadcn CSS variable; if a computed colour is genuinely needed, color-mix() over variables inside globals.css.
rules.why: anti-slop.md bans raw colour functions in components when a token system exists; the old gate covered hex and oklch but not these.

rules.title: No muted text paired with a muted background in one class string

detect.falsePositives: The pattern alone matches every legitimate muted-text usage — it is only a pre-filter. Findings come exclusively from the structural single-string check in token-rules.mjs; rulecheck routes this id there and never runs the pattern generically.

rules.fix: Give muted text a non-muted surface (bg-card, bg-background), or rebind [--muted-foreground:var(--accent-foreground)] on the surface-painting wrapper — note the rebind lives on the wrapper, never in the same class string as the pairing.
rules.why: bg-muted/accent/secondary with text-muted-foreground is 4.34:1 against a 4.5:1 minimum (a11y-baseline.md).

rules.title: No muted text/background split across a cva() base and a variant value

detect.falsePositives: Same pre-filter as TOK-4; findings come exclusively from the balanced-paren cva scan in token-rules.mjs (the shape that let components/ui/tabs.tsx ship the exact pairing this gate exists to catch).

rules.fix: Rebind [--muted-foreground:var(--accent-foreground)] on the variant that paints the surface.
rules.why: A base class and a variant value render together at runtime; the single-string rule cannot see the pair.

rules.title: Foreground composites only from foreground, only at the measured steps

detect.falsePositives: A comment or docs string naming a banned form rather than applying one — phrase prose as 'muted-foreground at 60% opacity', never the utility form (the GH-1234 convention; applied to calendar-view's history note when this rule landed). The size shorthand text-sm/6 is excluded by the pattern itself.

rules.fix: Quiet text derives from the foreground token at a pinned step — text-foreground/60, /70 or /80 (floor measured 2026-08-23: /60 ≥ 5.11:1 on every shipped surface, both themes). Below the floor, any other colour's composite, and arbitrary alphas: use the flat semantic token or TOK-6's rebind device instead.
rules.why: A composite resolves against whatever sits behind it, so neither the pair rules nor a story-scoped axe run reliably sees one. foreground/50 measures 3.65–3.71:1 in light (AA fail); composites of muted-foreground are strictly worse than its flat 4.34:1. The pinned set {60,70,80} is the live set and may only shrink — a new step is a rule change carrying a new measurement (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-23-foreground-opacity-floor-design.md).

rules.title: Only lucide-react ships icons in registry sources

detect.falsePositives: A non-icon package with 'icon' in its name, or a local module named icons. lucide-react contains no 'icon' substring, so the sanctioned library never matches.

rules.fix: Import the equivalent glyph from lucide-react at the size the component already uses (16/20/24).
rules.why: One library, one stroke weight (anti-slop.md): mixed icon sets read as unguided assembly. Closes the zero-homes gap left when the prose grep (old anti-slop Part 4 ICO-1) was retired. Inverted from a four-library denylist (final review): any icon-ish import that is not lucide-react now needs a look.

rules.title: Movement always carries a motion-reduce pair

detect.falsePositives: A pair set in a sibling cn() argument or in CSS under prefers-reduced-motion is not seen. The pattern is only a pre-filter; rulecheck routes this id to motion-rules.mjs.

rules.fix: Pair the animation with motion-reduce:animate-none or motion-reduce:transition-none in the same class string.
rules.why: Movement that ignores the OS reduced-motion setting fails the users who asked for less of it.
